intro: Need a visa for China? We handle your China visa application from start to finish: we complete the online form, check your documents, book your visa centre appointment and keep you updated until your visa is ready. Standard service from £301 in total, or express in 48 working hours.

sections.heading: Do you need a visa for China?
sections.text:
It depends on your passport, how long you’re staying and what you’re doing.

- British passport, trip of up to 30 days for tourism, business, family visits or transit: you don’t currently need a visa. This visa-free policy runs until 31 December 2026, and China hasn’t yet confirmed whether it will continue in 2027.
- Staying longer than 30 days, or going to work, study or report as a journalist: you need a visa.
- Living in the UK on another passport, such as Indian, Pakistani or Nigerian: you usually need a visa, whatever the length of your trip.

If you’re travelling in 2027, ask us before you book. If the visa-free policy isn’t extended, British travellers will need a visa again from 1 January 2027. See [China visa-free 2027](/blog/china-visa-free-2027/) for the latest.

sections.heading: How our China visa application service works
sections.text:
- Tell us about your trip using our online China visa application form, so we can confirm the right visa type
- We give you a document checklist and check everything you send against the visa centre’s requirements
- We complete the China online visa application form for you, so the details match your passport and documents exactly
- We book your appointment at the Chinese Visa Application Service Centre
- We keep you updated until your visa is ready and return your passport by your chosen delivery option, or you can collect it from our Manchester office

Most applications can be handled by post and email, so you don’t need to visit us in person.

sections.heading: Documents for a China visa application
sections.text:
Every China visa application needs:
- Your passport, valid for at least six months, with at least two blank visa pages
- A recent colour passport photo that meets the Chinese requirements
- The completed online application form, which we prepare for you
- Copies of any previous Chinese visas or Chinese passports
- Proof of legal residence in the UK if you aren’t a British citizen, such as your eVisa share code or BRP

Then, depending on your visa type:
- Tourist (L) visa: flight and hotel bookings, or an invitation from someone in China
- Business (M) visa: an invitation letter from the Chinese company or trade fair. Send them our free [China business invitation letter template](/downloads/china-business-invitation-letter-template.docx)
- Family (Q or S) visa: an invitation from your family member in China, with proof of your relationship and their status
- Work (Z) visa: your work permit notification from the Chinese employer

Need a photo? Our free [visa photo tool](/visa-photo-tool/?preset=china) sizes your photo for the China online form and makes a print sheet of 33 × 48 mm photos.

sections.heading: Which Chinese visa do you need?
sections.text:
The main visa types are:
- L visa: tourism
- M visa: business and trade
- Q1 and Q2 visas: visiting family members who are Chinese citizens or permanent residents
- S1 and S2 visas: visiting family members who are working or studying in China
- Z visa: work, with a work permit notification
- X1 and X2 visas: study

Choosing the right type and providing the matching invitation is the key to a smooth application. Use the trip chooser above, or ask us if you’re not sure.

sections.heading: China visa processing times
sections.text:
Once your application has been submitted at the visa centre:
- Standard service: about 5 working days
- Express service: about 48 working hours

Allow extra time for the appointment itself, especially around Chinese New Year and the summer holidays, when appointments get booked up. If your trip is urgent, call us and we’ll tell you the quickest realistic option.

sections.heading: UK residents with other passports
sections.text: The visa-free policy depends on your passport, not where you live. If you live in the UK on an Indian, Pakistani, Nigerian or other non-visa-free passport, you need a Chinese visa for any trip. Pakistani and Nigerian passport holders also need an invitation letter from China. We prepare applications for UK residents of all nationalities every week.

sections.heading: Chinese Visa Application Service Centre: London and Manchester
sections.text:
Every Chinese visa application from the UK is submitted in person at a Chinese Visa Application Service Centre (CVASC), where your fingerprints are taken. There are centres in London, Manchester, Edinburgh and Belfast. Which one you use depends on where you live, as each centre covers its own consular district. The Manchester centre only accepts applicants from its district.

- London centre: 12 Old Jewry, London EC2R 8DU (nearest tube: Bank)
- Manchester centre: Ground Floor, 71 Mosley Street, Manchester M2 3HR, a few doors from our office at 61 Mosley Street

We’re an independent, IAA-regulated adviser, not the official visa centre. The centre accepts and processes applications, but it doesn’t check whether your documents are strong enough or tell you which visa fits your trip. That’s what we do. We complete your online form, check every document and make sure you arrive with an application that won’t be sent back. Applying through the Manchester centre? Pop in to see us first, then walk round the corner to submit.

faqs.q: How much does a China visa application cost?
faqs.a: Our standard service costs £301 in total, made up of the £151 visa centre fee and our £150 fee. Express costs £357 in total. The visa centre fee can depend on your nationality and number of entries, so we confirm it before you pay.

faqs.q: How long does a China visa take from the UK?
faqs.a: About 5 working days with the standard service, or 48 working hours with express, once your application is submitted at the visa centre. Allow time for the appointment too.

faqs.q: Do British citizens need a visa for China?
faqs.a: Not for trips of up to 30 days for tourism, business, family visits or transit, until 31 December 2026. You still need a visa for longer stays, work or study, and for trips in 2027 if the policy isn’t extended.

faqs.q: Can you fill in the China visa application form for me?
faqs.a: Yes. We complete the China online visa application form for you and check every detail against your passport and documents before your appointment.

faqs.q: Do I need to go to the visa centre in person?
faqs.a: Usually yes, for fingerprints, unless you’re exempt. We book the appointment and make sure everything is ready, so the visit is quick.

The visa-free policy for British passports is due to end then unless China extends it. If it isn’t extended, you’ll need a visa for trips from 1 January 2027, so apply early if you’re travelling in January or February.

faqs.q: Which Chinese visa centre should I use?
faqs.a: The one that covers where you live. Each centre (London, Manchester, Edinburgh and Belfast) serves its own consular district, so it isn’t always the closest one. We’ll tell you which centre applies to you.

faqs.q: Is Unique Visa Services the Chinese visa centre?
faqs.a: No. We’re an independent, IAA-regulated visa adviser in Manchester. We prepare and check your application, and you then submit it and give your fingerprints at the official visa centre.
